Pipe material
Typical lifespan
50 years or more

Call (844) 212-9186

Rigid pipe, with a soldered joint at every turn.

What kind of pipe is in your walls?

Where it shows up

Common in homes built before the 1960s.

How to spot it

Gray, threaded pipe, often with rust-colored stains at the joints.

What goes wrong

It corrodes from the inside, which narrows the pipe. Pressure drops and water can turn brown.

What we recommend

Repiping is usually the lasting fix.

Do you need a repipe?

Tick anything that sounds familiar.

How a repipe runs

The length of the job depends on the size of your home. We give you a schedule with the quote, including when the water will be off.

  1. 1

    Inspection and quote

    We check the pipe material, condition and layout, then give you a written quote.

  2. 2

    Permit

    We pull the permit your city requires before any pipe comes out.

  3. 3

    Prep

    We protect floors and furniture, and tell you when the water will be off.

  4. 4

    New lines

    New pipe goes in through small access openings, not whole walls where we can avoid it.

  5. 5

    Test and inspection

    We pressure-test every line, and the city inspector signs off.

  6. 6

    Patch and clean up

    Access openings are patched and ready for paint.

Find out what your pipes are made of.

Call us for an inspection. You get a written report, your options in copper or PEX, and one clear quote.
